title: Will AI Slop and Deep fakes Kill Culture ? (Caroline Busta, Simon Denny, Marc Spiegler) | DLD26
description:
In this inspiring DLD Munich 2026 session, cultural strategist Marc Spiegler, artist Simon Denny and writer Caroline Busta wrestle with a deceptively simple question: will AI slop and deepfakes kill culture? 

Spiegler frames two competing scenarios. In the optimistic version, people hit a breaking point with low-quality, algorithmically driven content and swing back toward live experiences, in-person connection, and deeper focus. 

In the pessimistic version, the sludge wins: attention spans collapse, reading declines, and all that matters is how much dopamine our screens can deliver.

When Busta and Denny join the conversation, they broaden the perspective. Denny uses AI-generated imagery as raw material in his own art, mixing what he calls “sloppy outputs” with Italian Futurist paintings and defense-tech visuals to create something genuinely new – something he describes as “a way to synthesize the present in a new form.” 

Busta argues that slop is just another material, like oil paint or clay, and that real meaning-making now happens at the “protocol level“ – the decisions about how things are assembled, curated, and activated. 

She points to Charli XCX’s mockumentary “Brat” as an example: less an album than a protocol, a green screen that fans could project anything onto, where the audience co-creates the cultural moment. 

If you love thinking about how technology reshapes not just what we consume but how we make meaning, this video is for you.
